amber-hour-bottle:
Use case: product-mockup. One photorealistic 15 ml perfume bottle photograph.
Input 1 is the approved slim vial: exact physical identity to preserve. Input 2 is the ACTUAL AFTER BELLS WORDMARK ARTWORK: copy its precise letterforms, fine high-contrast serifs, spacing and proportions; use the artwork, not a substitute font.
Bottle identity: slender circular clear-glass vial, 8–9 times taller than its diameter, straight sides, thick rounded circular glass base, transparent gently curved dip tube. Small narrow CLOSED removable gold cap fitted above slightly wider fixed gold atomizer collar. No visible nozzle hole on a fitted cap. The cap and collar are MIRROR-POLISHED GLOSSY YELLOW GOLD, clean broad reflected softbox highlights and crisp reflective edges, never brushed, satin or matte.
Branding: apply the exact supplied "AFTER BELLS" wordmark directly to the long side of the GLASS in reflective metallic gold foil. Rotate the ENTIRE single-line wordmark 90 degrees counterclockwise, reading from base toward shoulder, with all letters sharing one baseline: sideways lettering along the bottle's long axis, NOT a stack of upright letters. It occupies ONLY 18–20 percent of the glass body's length, a tiny understated logo, less than half the size seen in earlier drafts, centred on the outward-facing side. Copy the reference artwork's exact typography. No opaque paper label, plaque or box. Add a SECOND SMALLER parallel line of reflective gold lettering beside the wordmark, reading exactly "AMBER HOUR", in clean delicate uppercase matching the fragrance-name lettering on the brand's original labels. This fragrance name runs in the SAME sideways bottom-to-top direction as the wordmark, centred alongside it and about half its length. Both lines form one very small restrained branding area. No other text. Gold foil conforms subtly to the cylindrical glass and catches real light; it is part of the product, never a floating graphic.
Gold flakes: realistic miniature scale. Approximately 20 tiny irregular wafer-thin foil flecks, mostly naturally settled in a very loose uneven trace just inside the base. Only 4–6 tiny wisps in the lower half. Most fragments 1–3 percent of VIAL DIAMETER, largest under 8 percent. Delicate torn edges, random orientation and physical depth. No oversized ribbons, butterflies, chunks, dense glitter, artificial sparkles or giant floating leaf shapes. Liquid remains mostly clear.
Keep small cap seam, meniscus, glass refraction, circular base and realistic contact shadow. No hands, other bottles, packaging, watermark, collage, captions or marketing typography.
Fragrance: AMBER HOUR. Liquid: transparent warm honey-amber, luminous golden in transmission, approximately 90% filled with a small air gap.
Main catalogue view: redesign a crisp full-length upright bottle portrait, front three-quarter just enough to see cylindrical volume while the gold sideways wordmark remains readable. One entire bottle centred, takes 78% of canvas height, generous calm margins, portrait 4:5, long lens, straight verticals. Scene: warm pale travertine ledge, sand-coloured architectural stone wall, late-afternoon light and a soft distant window shadow. Premium natural product photography, realistic softbox fill, no stylized render.
